# Invisible outline widths and shape text frames

Independent original OOXML controls generated by
`tools/hidden_outline_text_fixture.py`, using python-docx (MIT), lxml (BSD), and
standard Python libraries. No user template or font file is redistributed.
The reference application exported `native.pdf`; the reference generator records
source/PDF hashes, glyph colors, positions through raster crop bounds, and crops.

The 36 controls cross six text frames (top/center/bottom rectangles, a centered
ellipse, and overflowing center/bottom rectangles) with absent, zero, 2.25pt,
6pt, theme-inherited 2.25pt, and theme-overridden zero invisible line widths.
All use noFill for line paint. The reference application reserves half the effective line width
inside the text frame, despite drawing no stroke. Explicit zero overrides the
theme; an absent width with no theme contributes no inset. Width remains a
physical text inset, independent of the shape fill and paint bounds.

Before the fix, measured glyph origins differ by up to 3.025pt horizontally and
3.047pt vertically. Afterward, all 72 text lines (including case labels) match
within 0.030pt horizontally and 0.085pt vertically. Browser tests compare native
glyph coverage bidirectionally with two-pixel rasterization tolerance before
and after body editing/reopening; no-edit and undo package identity and unrelated
parts are checked. Unit tests also cover invalid active widths and preserved
scene semantics through export. There is no document-specific offset.

Specification context: DrawingML line width and style inheritance remain
separate from noFill paint (ECMA-376 Part 1 20.1.8.44); bodyPr text insets are
covered by 21.1.2.1.1. The half-line text inset, including invisible outlines,
is recorded as reference interoperability behavior demonstrated by these controls.
